post-install-output: * The core ships entities, not migrations. Write yours and run it: <comment>bin/console doctrine:migrations:diff</comment> then <comment>bin/console doctrine:migrations:migrate</comment>.
* Nobody can sign in yet. Add the first administrator with <comment>composer require --dev "uhifadhi/devkit-module:^0.1@dev"</comment> then <comment>bin/console team:user:create</comment>.

contents: # The areas — the ground: areas, their boundaries, the zones inside them, and
# the overview every module contributes to.
# THIS FILE IS EMPTY OF SETTINGS, AND THAT IS THE ANSWER. There is no `area:`
# key below because the areas have nothing an installation configures: what an
# area is called, where its boundary runs and which modules it runs are DATA,
# entered on the screens and kept in the database, never lines in a YAML file.
# Writing `area:` here with anything under it fails at compile time.
# What the areas DO need from this installation is a database, which
# config/packages/doctrine.yaml and DATABASE_URL supply, and a migration, which
# `doctrine:migrations:diff` writes. See the README.
# The file is kept so `config/packages/` has one entry per core bundle and
# nobody has to wonder whether the areas were forgotten.
# The atlas — the maps, charts and calendars every screen draws through, and the
# chrome they all wear.
# NOTHING BELOW IS REQUIRED; the tree is closed, so an invented key fails
# loudly. The one thing an installation usually wants to say is where satellite
# imagery comes from.
atlas:
satellite:
# esri   — keyless World Imagery. No account, no session, no key. The
#          default, and the understudy for both others: a map is never
#          blank for want of a key.
# google — the Map Tiles API. Set `google.api_key` (from an env var) and
#          name this provider to opt in.
# custom — your own XYZ/WMTS source. `custom.url_template` is then
#          REQUIRED, because a custom source with no url is a blank map
#          at 3am rather than an error at deploy time.
provider: esri
# Deepest zoom the satellite layer is asked for.
max_zoom: 19
#google:
#    # Public by nature — it travels in every tile URL. Restrict it by
#    # HTTP referrer at Google.
#    api_key: '%env(default::UHIFADHI_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY)%'
#custom:
#    url_template: 'https://tiles.example.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.jpg'
#    # The credit line the source's licence requires. Shown on every map
#    # that draws it.
#    attribution: 'Imagery © Example Mapping Agency'
# The registry — the runtime every uhifadhi module registers with: the
# catalogue of what this installation has, the record of what each area
# switched on, and the permissions modules declare.
# NOTHING BELOW IS REQUIRED. Every key has a default and the tree is closed, so
# an unknown key fails loudly rather than being ignored.
# THERE IS DELIBERATELY NO KEY LISTING MODULES. Installing a module IS the
# declaration, and a second place to enable one is a second place for the two to
# disagree. The catalogue reconciles itself with what is installed; there is no
# command to run.
registry:
# Where a module the catalogue cannot place is filed. A module hands its
# category over as a string and the registry coerces it, so a module written
# by somebody else can never break the catalogue with a typo.
default_category: operations
# The longest one SQL statement of a WEB REQUEST may run, in milliseconds,
# before PostgreSQL cancels it; 0 is no limit. Every connection opened
# under a web server API runs `SET statement_timeout` first; bin/console,
# the migrations and the queue worker never do. Keep the image's
# max_execution_time above it, so PHP is still there to report the
# cancelled statement. The typed env form an integer key takes:
# https://symfony.com/doc/current/configuration/env_var_processors.html
# https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/runtime-config-client.html#GUC-STATEMENT-TIMEOUT
statement_timeout_ms: '%env(int:DATABASE_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS)%'
# The queue the registry's work runs on: work a request hands over instead of
# doing, run by the worker (`php bin/console messenger:consume async
# scheduler_default`). Framework configuration from several files merges, so an
# installation's own config/packages/messenger.yaml — the one symfony/messenger's
# recipe writes — and this block make one `framework.messenger`.
# https://symfony.com/doc/current/configuration.html#configuration-files
# ONE TRANSPORT, IN THE DATABASE. MESSENGER_TRANSPORT_DSN is the Doctrine
# transport on the installation's own connection — the line symfony/messenger's
# recipe writes into .env, `doctrine://default?auto_setup=0`. Both queues are
# names in the one messenger_messages table, which the registry's migration
# creates (auto_setup=0: the schema is the migrations', never a request's). On
# PostgreSQL the transport notifies a waiting worker when a message lands.
# https://symfony.com/doc/current/messenger.html#doctrine-transport
# WHAT GOES ON IT is decided by the core: every message class that implements
# the core's queue marker is sent to `async`, because "You can also route
# classes by their parent class or interface."
# https://symfony.com/doc/current/messenger.html#routing-messages-to-a-transport
# (vendor/symfony/messenger/Transport/Sender/SendersLocator.php)
framework:
messenger:
# A message that has used up its retries is kept, not dropped —
# `messenger:failed:show` lists them, `messenger:failed:retry` runs
# them again. The default retry strategy stays: three retries, one
# second apart and doubling.
# https://symfony.com/doc/current/messenger.html#saving-retrying-failed-messages
failure_transport: failed
transports:
async:
dsn: '%env(MESSENGER_TRANSPORT_DSN)%'
options:
queue_name: async
failed:
dsn: '%env(MESSENGER_TRANSPORT_DSN)%'
options:
queue_name: failed
routing:
'Uhifadhi\Contracts\Queue\AsyncMessageInterface': async
# Dev-only tooling hangs off this flag, so a production installation never grows
# machinery that writes invented catalogue rows.
when@dev:
registry:
dev_tools: true
# Tests also send to memory, so a test can assert what was queued and nothing
# waits on a table: "Use in-memory:// in functional tests to verify correct
# message dispatch to transports".
# https://symfony.com/doc/current/messenger.html#in-memory-transport
when@test:
registry:
dev_tools: true
framework:
messenger:
transports:
async: 'in-memory://'
failed: 'in-memory://'
# The shell — what this installation looks like: the document, the page frame,
# the sidebar and top bar, and the theme every module's pages mount into.
# NOTHING BELOW IS REQUIRED. All three keys have defaults, and the tree is
# closed, so an unknown key fails loudly rather than being ignored. There is no
# database, no migration and no entity behind any of it — the shell draws, it
# does not remember.
# THERE IS DELIBERATELY NO KEY LISTING NAV ENTRIES, AREA TABS OR MODULES. Those
# arrive as data through the shell's contracts, because a nav declared in YAML
# is a nav no permission check ever reaches.
shell:
# The wordmark beside the brand mark in the sidebar. Yours to change: the
# shell cannot know what this installation calls itself.
brand_name: Uhifadhi
# Where the brand mark links. The shell is installed BY an application and
# cannot know its route names, so it takes one. `welcome` is the route
# config/routes/shell.yaml mounts at `/`; point this at your own home screen
# when you have one.
home_route: welcome
# What a visitor who has NEVER chosen a theme gets: light, dark, or `system`
# to honour what their operating system already says. All three are real
# answers — `system` is not a synonym for light.
# Whatever this says, the choice is applied by an inline script in the
# document head, BEFORE the first paint, so nobody is shown the wrong
# palette for a frame. A link may override it for one view with `?theme=dark`.
default_theme: light
# The team — people: accounts, positions, departments, and the screens somebody
# signs in, resets a password or accepts an invitation through.
# NONE OF THESE FOUR KEYS IS SECURITY. Who may reach what, how long a session
# lives, whether there is a remember-me cookie: that is config/packages/security.yaml,
# which this installation owns. What is here is what the SCREENS and the LETTERS
# need and a firewall has no opinion about.
# The tree is closed, so an invented key fails loudly.
team:
# Where a visitor who asks for /login while already signed in is sent. A
# path, not a route name — the team cannot know what your home screen is
# called.
after_sign_in_path: /
# The sentence under the mark on the sign-in card.
sign_in_lede: 'Analytical observatory for protected areas. Sign in to reach this installation and its modules.'
# The address invitations and password-reset links come from. EMPTY MEANS
# THIS INSTALLATION CANNOT SEND: the invite path is then offered and refused
# in writing, and the forgot-password screen says so rather than swallowing
# the request. Set it, and set MAILER_DSN in .env.local, before you invite
# anybody.
mail_from: ''
# What an email calls this installation in its subject line.
installation_name: Uhifadhi
# The area screens: the register, an area's overview, its zones, its settings
# and the grid where an administrator switches modules on and off for it.
# The addresses are the controllers' own, declared as attributes beside the code
# that answers them. This file is what mounts them, and it is yours.
# Every module renders under `/areas/{uuid}/modules/<its slug>`, and a module
# mounts its own routes through its own file beside this one. Nothing here has
# to change when a module arrives.
area:
resource: '@AreaBundle/Controller/'
type: attribute
# The shell's route — one line, and it is yours.
# The shell ships one route: the welcome page, named `welcome`, at `/` — the one
# screen a fresh installation has before it has grown one of its own. The core
# DEFINES it and loads it nowhere. This import is what makes it reachable, and
# this file belongs to YOUR application.
# THAT IS THE WHOLE OF THE SHELL'S CLAIM ON A URL, and withdrawing it is one
# edit. The day this installation has a real home screen, point `/` at it here —
# or delete this file and let whichever module owns the front door claim the
# address. Nothing in the shell depends on the route name or on the route
# existing; nothing is left behind.
# `debug:router` shows what you are replacing.
shell:
resource: '@ShellBundle/config/routes/welcome.php'
# The configure pages — the area's and every module's, one frame the shell owns.
shell_configure:
resource: '@ShellBundle/config/routes/configure.php'
# The team's screens: signing in and out, the password reset, accepting an
# invitation, the people register, positions and departments, and the endpoint a
# field client asks for a token at.
# The addresses are the controllers' own, declared as attributes beside the code
# that answers them. This file is what mounts them, and it is yours: unmount a
# screen by removing this import, and it is gone from `debug:router` with
# nothing left behind.
# WHO MAY REACH THEM IS NOT DECIDED HERE. config/packages/security.yaml puts
# everything behind sign-in and names the three of these a stranger must reach
# (`/login`, `/reset-password`, `/invite/…`); what a signed-in person may DO on
# them is checked in the controllers.
team:
resource: '@TeamBundle/Controller/'
type: attribute
